newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong marks last RAF Battle of Britain parade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong marks last RAF Battle of Britain parade.

text.p: The Royal Air Force in Hong Kong marked victory over the Germans in the 1940 air Battle of Britain for the last time on Sunday before the colony is handed back to China in mid-1997.
The event also marked the close of a chapter of RAF history. The Sek Kong air force base, the last RAF base in Asia, will be shut down in the next two months in preparation for the handover.

Hong Kong will return to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, ending more than 150 years as a colony. Military bases used by the British forces will be handed to communist China's People's Liberation Army.

Under the eyes of Commander British Forces in Hong Kong Major-General Bryan Dutton and Air Vice-Marshal Terry Sherrington, four Wessex helicopters of the RAF 28 squadron made a flypast over its base in the rural New Territories.
The two generals also inspected a 24-man parade and saluted as the RAF ensign was lowered for the last time.
"It's a sad day but it's also a proud day," Dutton told reporters after the commemoration.
"The RAF in Sek Kong has supported Hong Kong magnificently since the 1920s. They have done some very brave acts here," he said.
Hong Kong was the first base the RAF set up in Asia in 1927. After the closure of the Sek Kong base, the 28 squadron will operate from Hong Kong's international airport, Kai Tak, until June 30.
The German air force launched an invasion of Britain in 1940. The RAF repelled the Luftwaffe in the skies over England in what has become known as the Battle of Britain.
